name: Meter
purpose: A SINGLE COMPONENT FOR A VALUE ON A TRACK BETWEEN A MINIMUM AND A MAXIMUM. Progress-bar and Limits-meter roll up into it: progress becomes one SEMANTIC VARIANT of a meter rather than the identity of the component. ✅ ACCEPTED #210 — s210-D1, Dave verbatim: 'keep as one meter'. FIVE rulings are ENACTED in this component (s210-D1 unification, s210-D2 default title SMALL, s210-D3 no fixed width on the molecule, s210-D4 per-payment empty row dropped from the payment-limits organism, s210-D5 the CATALOGUE FOLD — Option C) and Q4 is answered (all three organisms ship). ✅ THE FOLD IS ENACTED AT THE CATALOGUE LAYER: progress-bar.meta.json and limits-meter.meta.json are now THIN CATEGORY ALIASES of this file, which is the ONE home of the spec (see $categoryIdentities). ⛔ STILL NOT GATED AND NOT PROMOTED — promotion, placement in gen_showroom.py CATEGORIES and component-types.json registration are Dave's and were not touched.
$daveVerbatim: The authority for this component is Dave's own words at #210, carried verbatim and not paraphrased: "if these are the base components we just have progress variants, also I would like the option of the bigger titles that are in the progress bar. Again what we have is a set of meter variants embedded in an organism, in this case a daily transfer limit lock-up." The grammar is his molecule -> organism model: a base Meter molecule, a set of variants of which progress is one, and organism specimens that embed those variants — the daily-transfer-limit lock-up being the one he named.

$categoryIdentities.$ruling: s210-D5 (Dave, #210: 'C looks good to me, all works'). ONE MOLECULE, TWO SELECTABLE IDENTITIES. The full spec lives HERE and only here; the two identities are thin ALIAS metas that hold no spec and structurally cannot drift from it. This is the memo's Option C, whose whole argument is that sentence: 'No duplicated spec prose exists to drift, because the aliases hold no spec.'

progress.$whenYouWantIt: The value is a task underway and a FULL bar means DONE: uploads, downloads, multi-part transfers, savings goals, completeness scores.

allowance.$whenYouWantIt: The value is a cap you are spending against and a FULL bar means BLOCKED, not done: payment / daily / monthly transfer limits, card spending caps.

$categoryIdentities.$audience: AUTHORING-TIME, and that is the point. Dave's requirement, verbatim: 'For me the user, selecting the component, AI model or human need to understand the difference even though the physical shape might be the same.' A human browsing the store and a model retrieving a component both hit a named identity that routes to this one spec; a screen-reader user is NOT this audience, which is the reason the ARIA role was NOT split (see accessibility.roleDecision).
$categoryIdentities.$placement: ⬛ NOT PLACED, and declared rather than smoothed. gen_showroom.py CATEGORIES has no meter bucket, so meter, progress-bar, limits-meter and runway-bar all still fall through to the uncategorised 'More' tail. The memo says in terms that where the two readings go is 'a call this memo does not make'; placement is promotion and promotion is Dave's. The identities are authored and retrievable today; their SHELF is empty.

props.name: shape
props.$note: Linear for inline/full-width meters; dial for a compact circular readout. Both are Progress-bar's, copied — the dial is its 96px ring with an 8px stroke and the role on the visible numeric caption.

props.name: size
props.$note: Linear only: 4px track (default) or 8px (emphasis). Progress-bar's own two sizes and its same token pair, which Limits-meter already inherited. Nothing new. The dial is a single 96px specimen; further rungs need a ruling, not an invention.

props.name: titleSize
props.$note: ✅ RULED s210-D2 (#210, Dave verbatim: 'default small'). THE DEFAULT IS NO LONGER A PLACEHOLDER — it is his ruling. 'default' = t-cm-legal, 12px, text/secondary — the row-name treatment the Limits-meter stack uses — and it carries NO modifier class. 'large' = t-cm-label, 16px, text/default — Progress-bar's own title treatment — is the EXPLICIT OPT-IN modifier .meter--title-lg, which is the option Dave asked for in so many words: 'the option of the bigger titles that are in the progress bar'. The SIZE is carried by the composite class in the markup (type is bound by composite, never by a raw declaration); the .meter--title-lg modifier carries only the colour difference the two parents already disagree about. Both stay drawn on the same meter in §B6 of the reference as the RECEIPT for the ruling, not as an open choice.

props.name: semantics
props.$note: ✅ RULED s210-D5 (#210, Dave verbatim: 'C looks good to me, all works' — Option C of the categorical-split memo). THESE TWO WORDS ARE THE CATEGORY IDENTITIES, and Q6's vocabulary question is closed on them: 'progress' and 'allowance' are what the catalogue selects by, carried by the two alias metas (progress-bar.meta.json reading 'progress', limits-meter.meta.json reading 'allowance'). They still paint NOTHING different, deliberately: the geometry is identical and the meaning is inverted — a full progress meter is SUCCESS, a full allowance meter is a BLOCKED PAYMENT. The split Dave ruled is a CATALOGUE-LEVEL one ('even if it's only categorical'), so the difference is legible at SELECTION time and authored in the markup, not painted.

props.name: value
props.$note: Current value on the min..max scale. Drives both the visual fill and aria-valuenow.

props.name: max
props.$note: Under 'allowance' semantics this is the CEILING, not a target. ⛔ A target is a goal you are trying to reach; a cap is a boundary you are not allowed to cross. A meter that grows a target IS a Chart-bullet.

props.name: label
props.$note: The accessible name. Required — a meter with no name announces only a number.

props.name: valueText
props.$note: Human-readable value for AT (aria-valuetext). Required whenever the scale is not a plain percentage — '1,450 pounds of 2,000 pounds saved', '3,200 pounds used of a 5,000 pound daily transfer limit'.

props.name: showValue
props.$note: Renders the numeric value as visible text. Default TRUE and load-bearing, not decoration: it is what carries meaning independently of the fill/track boundary (1.4.1). Progress-bar's own reasoning, inherited.

variants.name: linear
variants.use: The base: a 4px rule that fills. Progress-bar specimen 1, copied.

variants.name: emphasis
variants.use: An 8px rule where the meter is the primary content of its region. Progress-bar's .pb-lg / Limits-meter's .lim-lg, same token pair.

variants.name: non-percentage scale
variants.use: A domain scale carried in aria-valuetext — the 'Savings goal · 1,450 of 2,000' bar. Progress-bar specimen 3, copied. ★ This is the specimen the whole overlap argument turns on: geometrically it is already a limits meter, and progress-bar.meta.json's commonPatterns names 'savings goal / limits meter' by name.

variants.name: dial
variants.use: The circular form — a compact completeness score where a full-width rule would not fit. Progress-bar specimen 4, copied.

variants.name: allowance
variants.use: The limits reading: how much of a cap is used, with a compact two-key readout. Limits-meter specimen 5, copied. Same geometry as emphasis; the difference is entirely one of meaning.

variants.name: title-size
variants.use: The two title treatments drawn on the same meter, side by side — the option Dave asked for. ✅ RULED s210-D2: SMALL is the default and needs no class; the large title is the opt-in .meter--title-lg. §B6 keeps the pair as the receipt.

variants.name: empty
variants.use: Value at the minimum — a 0% fill. ADDED at #210 as §B7. It exists because s210-D4 dropped the empty per-payment row from ONE organism and the ruling's own scope sentence keeps the STATE legal: 'an empty meter remains a legal state'. Drawn on the bare molecule so the drop cannot be misread as a retirement.

$organisms.name: daily-transfer-limit lock-up
$organisms.use: DAVE'S OWN EXAMPLE. A title, a verdict chip, a display figure, ONE meter molecule, a legend and — at the ceiling — a consequence sentence. Drawn in §C1 (within limit) and §C2 (at limit). Limits-meter specimens 1 and 3, copied. ⛔ The lock-up is NOT a meter; the meter is the part inside it that has a value.

$organisms.name: payment-limits set
$organisms.use: TWO meter molecules in one organism under ONE group label — per day, per month, no chips. Drawn in §C3. Limits-meter specimen 4, copied. This is the clearest reading of 'a set of meter variants embedded in an organism'. ⚑ s210-D4 ENACTED (#210, Dave: 'Per payment seems redundant in this context'): the third row — the per-payment EMPTY track reading '£0 of £10,000 used', which never accumulates because a per-payment cap is a ceiling PER EVENT — IS REMOVED. Its rule is not lost: it is restated as a sentence in the organism's caption, because a per-event ceiling is a stated RULE and not a quantity. ⛔ SCOPE: the drop is THIS ORGANISM'S only; an empty meter remains a legal state (see the 'empty' variant / §B7).

$organisms.name: savings-goal lock-up
$organisms.use: ✅ DRAWN at #210 as §C4 on Dave's Q4 answer, verbatim: 'I think we have all three, just be careful, dont hand roll, use the atoms.' A title, an on-track chip, a display figure, ONE progress-semantics meter (the §B3 savings-goal bar, values unchanged) and a two-key legend. ⛔ ZERO NEW CSS: every class is one this component already defines and uses in §C1 and §B3 — .lockup, .lockup-head, .lockup-title, .chip.ok, .amount.amount--display, .meter-verdict, .meter, .meter-track, .meter-fill, .meter-legend, .meter-key, .sw. ⛔ IT DRAWS NO CARD CHROME: no border, no surface, no radius, no padding is invented, because Card is a SEPARATE component that would wrap this lock-up, and inventing card chrome here is exactly the #202 defect Dave's own 'dont hand roll' warns against. This is the one organism where a FULL meter is SUCCESS — a savings goal is a target reached, not an allowance spent.

tokens.fill: progress/complete — the filled part. THEME INK in all four themes since s175-D1, exactly as both parents bind it.
tokens.text: text/default — figures, the large title option, the consequence line
tokens.muted: text/secondary — the default title, labels, legend keys, captions
tokens.border: border/subtle — the outline on the 'left' legend swatch, so an empty swatch is still a visible mark
tokens.status: rag/success + rag/success-tint | rag/warning + rag/warning-tint — the ORGANISM's verdict chip only, copied byte-for-byte from Limits-meter via Runway-bar and Account-card. ⛔ NO RAG VALUE TOUCHES A TRACK OR A FILL IN ANY VARIANT OR ANY STATE.
tokens.radius: border-radius/indicator — 0; the angular rule, console forks through the cascade. Nothing is round except the 8px chip dot and the dial, which is round because it is a ring.
tokens.$note: NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED AND NO NEW COLOUR VALUE IS AUTHORED. Every hex in the reference is copied from Progress-bar or Limits-meter. See $noRedInvented.

$noRedInvented: ⛔ THE LAW THIS COMPONENT INHERITS AND DOES NOT TOUCH. A meter at 100% is where a critical red gets improvised, and none is. The fill is INK ON TRACK in every variant and every state, including the at-limit organism, inherited from the gated Progress-bar whose meta gives the reason in Dave's terms: 'Progress is STRUCTURE, not status (Dave 2026-07-21) — hence the ink pair rather than a RAG colour.' A task half-done and an allowance half-spent are both QUANTITIES. The VERDICT is a separate object belonging to the ORGANISM — a Status-indicator RAG-tint chip carrying a WORD and a reset time — and which verdict maps to which tint is a SEMANTIC binding that is DAVE'S, proposed not ruled. The error/critical seat is NOT taken even at the ceiling: that touches the two-red law (s151-D1) and the mono error ink camp (s149-D1), neither of which this file goes near.

motion.entry: The fill's width transition (linear) and the ring's stroke-dashoffset transition (dial), over the inherited 140ms ease.
motion.reducedMotion: The fill still MOVES to its final position — the value must be reachable — it just arrives without an animated sweep (2.3.3 / 2.2.2). Both parents' behaviour, copied, plus the global collapse Limits-meter carries.

responsive.rule: ✅ RULED s210-D3 (#210, Dave verbatim: 'They should be responsive teh container dictates teh width'). THE MOLECULE DECLARES NO WIDTH. max-width is REMOVED from .meter and, for the same reason, from .lockup and .lockup-stack: the meter is 100% of whatever box it is put in, and the containing organism or page layout owns the width. The two parents' disagreement (Progress-bar 420px, Limits-meter 480px) is MOOT — neither figure is carried. Any width visible in a specimen is the SPECIMEN'S DEMO CHROME (.demo-col / .demo-w-* / .demo-frame, commented as such and referenced by no .meter-* rule); §A2 of the reference draws the same meter in 320 / 640 / 1180 demo containers so the ruling is seen rather than read. Heads and legends still wrap. The dial is a fixed 96px and does not reflow — it is a ring, not a rule. No breakpoint switch and no container query.

mustNotNeighbour: Loading indicator for the same task (one claims the duration is known, the other that it is not)
A Chart-bullet showing the same value against a target (a limit is not a target)
A second meter restating the same number in the opposite direction

accessibility.role: role="progressbar" on every track and on the dial's visible numeric caption, with aria-valuenow / valuemin / valuemax and a domain-carrying aria-valuetext; role="group" + aria-labelledby around each organism; role="status" on the at-limit consequence sentence. All mirrored from the two parents.
accessibility.roleDecision: ✅ RULED s210-D5 (#210, Dave picked Option C, which the memo paired with keeping the role): role="progressbar" STAYS ON EVERY METER, IN BOTH READINGS. role="meter" is NOT adopted. THE REASONS, written down as a DECISION so a future session does not re-litigate it a fourth time: (1) the categorical requirement is an AUTHORING-time one — a screen-reader user reads a value, they do not select a component, so splitting the role would serve the wrong audience for the need Dave stated; (2) the user-facing meaning is already carried better, by the visible value plus a domain-words aria-valuetext ('3,200 pounds used of a 5,000 pound daily transfer limit, leaving 1,800 pounds. Resets at midnight.'), in every screen reader, today; (3) role="meter" (ARIA 1.1) has historically WEAK and inconsistent AT support where progressbar is universal. ⚠ TWO HONEST LIMITS, DECLARED NOT SMOOTHED: the support facts are general accessibility knowledge, NOT a measurement made in this repo — the memo flagged this and the check was NOT done, so this ruling carries a RE-CHECK, not permanence: re-verify role="meter" support against current tables at the next accessibility sweep (owner: Dave/conductor to schedule) and re-put the question if the picture has changed. And it leaves a component literally called Meter using role="progressbar" — that is the accepted consequence, not an oversight.
accessibility.$openRoleQuestionHISTORICAL: ⚠ SUPERSEDED BY s210-D5, kept as the record of the moment it was true. AS WRITTEN AT THE #210 BUILD PASS: ⚠ UNRULED, MIRRORED, NOT DECIDED HERE (Q3). role="progressbar" vs role="meter". The search that fails to settle it was RE-RUN at #210 rather than cited (s202-D3): `grep -rln 'role="meter"' knowledge/snippets/` → THREE files (Limits-meter, Runway-bar and Meter) and EVERY hit in all three is PROSE not markup, i.e. ZERO snippets use the role; `grep -icE '\bmeter\b' knowledge/_rulings.json` → 0. Nothing in the store rules it either way. progressbar is used because BOTH parents carry it and inheriting beats improvising. ⚠ THE QUESTION IS SHARPER NOW, NOT SOFTER — the component is literally called Meter. DAVE'S; if he rules 'meter', THREE files change together.
accessibility.circularNaming: On the dial the role sits on the VISIBLE numeric caption and the svg is aria-hidden, so the accessible name and the on-screen value are the same object and nothing is announced twice. Progress-bar's own choice, copied.
accessibility.notColourAlone: Every meter renders its value as text and carries aria-valuetext; every organism additionally carries a verdict WORD in its chip and, at the ceiling, a consequence sentence. Remove all colour and the component still says everything it means (1.4.1).
accessibility.hitArea: PASSIVE — the component contains no interactive target, so the 44px minimum has no seat here. Declared rather than assumed.

antiPatterns: ⛔ PAINTING THE FILL RED AT THE CEILING. Ink on track in every variant and every state. See $noRedInvented.
⛔ GROWING A TARGET MARKER OR QUALITATIVE BANDS. With a target this IS a Chart-bullet and should be one.

⛔ WRITING SPEC INTO THE TWO ALIAS METAS. progress-bar.meta.json and limits-meter.meta.json are thin category aliases of THIS file (s210-D5) and hold no props, tokens, variants, antiPatterns, accessibility or tokenValidation of their own — the schema's aliasOf seat refuses them and probe_meta_schema.py is the consumer that says so. Two documents describing one artefact WILL drift; that is exactly what Option C was picked to prevent. See $foldEnacted.
Using this for work of unknown duration — that is Loading indicator. There is deliberately no indeterminate variant, inherited from Progress-bar's scope fence (s173-D1).
Omitting the accessible name, which leaves AT announcing a number with no subject.
Using aria-valuenow on a non-percentage scale without aria-valuetext.
Putting role=progressbar on the decorative svg as well as on its caption — the value is then announced twice.
Adding a focus indicator or tabindex: a meter reports, it does not accept input.
Relying on the chip DOT to convey a verdict. The dot is 1.98:1 / 2.18:1 standalone (measured #204); the word is the carrier.
Painting a delta or an arrow on this component. The two delta conventions question is OPEN AND DAVE'S and nothing here may settle it by construction.

$differsFrom.Progress-bar: PROPOSED PARENT-OF. Progress-bar's entire surface is reproduced here as VARIANTS — linear 4px, emphasis 8px, non-percentage scale, dial — copied declaration-for-declaration and markup-for-markup. Nothing of it is lost and nothing of it is changed. What moves is the FRAMING: under this proposal 'progress' is a semantic variant of a meter rather than the identity of the component, which is Dave's own sentence, 'we just have progress variants'. ⛔ Progress-bar remains GATED, PROMOTED and BYTE-UNTOUCHED until he rules.
$differsFrom.Limits-meter: PROPOSED PARENT-OF. Its readout becomes the ORGANISM section — the daily-transfer-limit lock-up and the payment-limits set, both composed of meter molecules — plus the 'allowance' semantic variant and the compact two-key readout. Its own head comment already argued that a bare limits meter IS a progress bar and should be one; this proposal is the constructive form of that argument. ⛔ Limits-meter remains BYTE-UNTOUCHED until he rules.
$differsFrom.Chart-bullet: Unchanged from the Limits-meter adjudication: a TARGET is a goal you are trying to reach, a LIMIT is a ceiling you are not allowed to cross. No target marker, no qualitative bands, no SVG figure, no dv-table, no dataviz series token. A meter that grows a target IS a Chart-bullet.
$differsFrom.Runway-bar: NOT MERGED AND NOT ASSUMED — deliberately out of scope. Runway asks 'does my money cover what is scheduled, and until when?' (max = my balance, horizon = a date discovered); an allowance meter asks 'how much am I allowed to move, and when does it come back?' (max = a cap, horizon = a repeating reset). Whether Runway-bar is a third semantic variant of this same meter is a REAL question, and it is not put here: this file's scope is the two components Dave named.
